vehicle_type.intro:
Please first mount your vehicle with wheels OFF the ground.

Then choose your **frame class** and select everything **that is true for your vehicle**.

All following steps depend on these answers.
vehicle_type.help:
**Vehicle info** is read from the flight controller whenever this step opens.

**Frame class**: *Rover* for wheeled vehicles, *Boat* for boats. A change needs a **reboot** (offered at the end of Phase 1).

**Sails**: ArduPilot can sail boats and land yachts; *Vehicle has sails* switches its sailing support on (`SAIL_ENABLE`, then reboot) and shows the Sails and Wind vane steps. A sailing vehicle may also have a motor - without one, the drive tests that need throttle are skipped.

**Too heavy to rotate**: check this if the vehicle can't realistically be picked up and rotated by hand; the Compass calibration step will then offer **Large Vehicle MagCal** (enter a known heading) instead of the usual rotate-by-hand calibration.

The wizard detects a firmware version and hides parameters that do not exist on your version. Every change the wizard makes is recorded and can be reverted; the parameter list (**Ctrl+P**) has **Backup** (every parameter into a file) and **Restore** (write a file's values back).

Progress and measurements are saved in the wizard's data folder (Linux: `~/.local/share/rover-wizard` or `$XDG_DATA_HOME/rover-wizard`, macOS: `~/Library/Application Support/rover-wizard`, Windows: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\rover-wizard`), so you can stop any time and continue later.

**Optional hardware**: ArduPilot Rover runs without GPS, compass, RC receiver, etc. Each checkbox starts from what the vehicle's parameters say is configured. Unchecking one hides the steps for it and, where a single parameter does it, switches the device off so pre-arm checks don't wait for it.

**Changes need a reboot.**

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/HardwareReport> to get a detailed hardware report of your vehicle in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/apmrover-setup.html>

steering_output.intro: Choose the **steering type**; for front-wheel steering, assign the steering servo output and confirm its direction.
steering_output.help:
**Steering type**

* **Front-wheel steering (Ackermann)**: a steering servo and a throttle/ESC output, like an RC car.
* **Skid steering**: two independently driven left/right throttles like a tank. There is no steering servo, so this step only asks for the type.

The flight controller needs to know which SERVO/MAIN output drives the steering servo; a change of output channel needs a **reboot** (offered at the end of Phase 1); the wizard writes `SERVOx_FUNCTION=26` for you and clears it from any other output.

**LIFT THE WHEELS OFF THE GROUND** before testing. *Test L*/*Test R* hold the steering stick left/right by the *test deflection* for a few seconds - the vehicle stays disarmed, since Rover moves the steering servo while disarmed. The *+*/*-* buttons next to MIN/MAX/TRIM change the value immediately and move the servo to it the same way. If it moves the wrong way, check **Reverse output**.

MIN/MAX/TRIM set the servo's mechanical end stops and centre position.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>

motor_output.intro: Choose the motor driver signal, assign the throttle/motor output(s), confirm their direction, and find the throttle dead-zone - with the **wheels OFF the ground**.
motor_output.help:
**Motor driver / ESC signal** (MOT_PWM_TYPE): *Normal* for hobby ESCs and servos, *Brushed* types for H-bridge motor drivers (then also set the PWM frequency), *DShot* for DShot ESCs. A change needs a **reboot**.

The flight controller needs to know which SERVO/MAIN output(s) drive the motor(s); the wizard writes `SERVOx_FUNCTION` for you (70 throttle, or 73/74 left/right for skid steering) and clears it from any other output.

**LIFT THE WHEELS OFF THE GROUND** before testing. *Test ↑*/*Test ↓* run the motor briefly forward/reverse with ArduPilot's motor test. Note: the motor test **arms the vehicle** for its duration and disarms it afterwards; it needs calibrated RC, the safety switch pressed and passing arming checks. Start it disarmed. If a wheel turns the wrong way, check **Reverse output**.

**Dead-zone**: motors often need some power before they move. *Probe* next to *Minimum throttle* ramps the power; press Continue when the wheel starts turning - the value is proposed as **MOT_THR_MIN** (press Apply to keep it).

MOT_THR_MAX limits full power, MOT_SLEWRATE limits how fast throttle may change (%/s), MOT_STR_THR_MIX (skid only) sets how much of the throttle range steering may use.

A change of output channel needs a **reboot** (offered at the end of Phase 1).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>

orientation.intro: Tell the autopilot how the flight-controller board is mounted in the vehicle or autoprobe it.
orientation.help:
**AHRS_ORIENTATION**: rotation of the flight controller relative to the vehicle's forward/right/down. Leave *None* if the arrow on the board points forward. A wrong value makes heading and turning unusable.

**Probe**: automatically determines this by resetting orientation, rebooting, reading the accelerometer level and then nose-down, and matching the readings against every possible mounting. Needs two reboots (vehicle disarmed) and takes about a minute.

This step comes before the calibrations on purpose: ArduPilot's documentation requires AHRS_ORIENTATION to be set before the accelerometer calibration, and the compass calibration needs both.

Changing the orientation after the *Level calibration* makes that calibration's level reference (AHRS_TRIM) wrong: the wizard says so and opens the Accelerometer & gyro step again - redo the Level calibration after the reboot. The 6-position calibration stays valid.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-mounting-the-flight-controller.html>

gps.intro: Configure the GPS receiver(s): type, serial port and baud rate, antenna position, and how two receivers are used.
gps.help:
**Number of GPS receivers**: ArduPilot supports two. With two, choose which one to configure and how they are used: *Use best* picks the better receiver, *Blend* combines two identical receivers.

**GPS type**: *Auto* works for most u-blox receivers but never tries NMEA. **Probe** tries Auto first, then NMEA, rebooting after each attempt; ArduPilot finds the receiver's baud rate by itself, so the probe waits for its full round of baud rates.

**Serial port** and **baud rate**: where the receiver is wired. **Antenna offset**: position relative to the vehicle's centre of gravity (X forward, Y right, Z down, metres).

*Show GPS status* watches fix and satellite count (needs a view of the sky). Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-positioning-landing-page.html>

accel.help:
**Gyro**: keep the vehicle still. **Level**: sets the 'flat' reference (AHRS trim) - do it with the vehicle on flat ground in its driving attitude. **6-position accel calibration**: the flight controller asks for LEVEL, LEFT, RIGHT, NOSE DOWN, NOSE UP and BACK; place the vehicle accordingly and press Continue each time. Do the 6-position calibration once per vehicle, level calibration whenever the mounting changed.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/FilterReview> and <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/FilterTool> to review/configure gyro noise filter settings in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-accelerometer-calibration.html>

compass.intro: Calibrate the compass by rotating the vehicle - or, for heavy vehicles, from a known heading.
compass.help:
The onboard calibration runs on the flight controller. Hold the vehicle in the air (it is small enough) and rotate it so every side points to the ground. Keep it away from metal, speakers, motors and cables with high current. **Fitness** (lower is better; values up to about 10-15 are fine). *External compass orientation* must match how the external compass module is mounted (if any). Auto declination uses the GPS position for the local magnetic declination.

**Large Vehicle MagCal** (shown because you checked *too heavy to rotate* on the Frame step): instead of rotating the vehicle, park it still and enter its current heading relative to **true north** (e.g. read from a phone compass app in true-north mode, or a known landmark bearing). ArduPilot computes the calibration in one shot from the World Magnetic Model at the vehicle's GPS location - needs a 3D GPS fix.

**Orientation of an external compass**: the rotate-by-hand calibration detects it by itself (*Detect orientation during calibration*). Large Vehicle MagCal can't - it needs the orientation set first: **Probe** next to *External compass orientation* finds it from two headings (front to magnetic north, then south; needs two reboots).

**Motor interference compensation** (shown when the battery monitor reports a current - set it up on the *Battery monitor* step just before, and reboot after changing the monitor type): current in the motors, ESC and power wires adds its own magnetic field, so the heading drifts while driving. *Measure compass-motor interference* runs the motors with the wheels lifted and measures how much the compass reading changes per amp; ArduPilot then subtracts that (COMPASS_MOTCT = *Use current*). Do it after the compass calibration, and again after moving the compass or re-routing power wires.

**Compasses found / Use compass n**: every compass the flight controller detected, internal or external, and the order ArduPilot uses them in. On a rover the internal compass sits close to motors and power wires; if an external compass is fitted, setting the internal one to *Not used* usually gives a steadier heading. At least one compass must stay in use. (ArduPilot switches compasses by their priority - COMPASS_USE / USE2 / USE3 follow COMPASS_PRIO1..3_ID, not the detection order; the wizard picks the right one.)

**Declination** (shown without a GPS, or with *Automatic declination* off): the angle between true and magnetic north where you drive, east positive. ArduPilot can only look it up from its position; without one it uses this value - leaving it at 0 turns every heading by the local declination.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/MAGFit> to calibrate the compass from flight logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-calibration-in-mission-planner.html>

barometer.intro: Check the barometer(s) the flight controller found, and set up an external one.
barometer.help:
Almost every flight controller has a barometer on board. ArduPilot finds its barometers at every boot and measures the ground pressure then - there is nothing to calibrate. A rover uses the barometer for the EKF's height estimate (*Position sources (EKF)* step: vertical position from the barometer is the default) and for the *Barometer* pre-arm check.

**Barometers found** lists them in ArduPilot's order (barometer 1 = `BARO1_DEVID`, reported in `SCALED_PRESSURE`; barometer 2 in `SCALED_PRESSURE2`, ...). **Show pressure** logs what each one measures and whether ArduPilot considers them healthy - a working barometer shows a steady pressure (about 1013 hPa at sea level, less higher up) and a plausible temperature.

**PreArm: Baro: not healthy**: usually gone after a reboot; if it stays, the sensor (or a long I2C cable to an external one) is faulty. A board without any barometer reports *Baro: unable to initialise driver*: it needs an external one.

**External barometer** (e.g. to get it away from air pressure disturbances, or for a board without one): connect it to an I2C port, tick *An external barometer is connected* and the sensor's type, Apply and reboot. It then appears in the list; choose it under *Barometer to use*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>

rc.intro: Map and calibrate the transmitter channels and assign flight modes.
rc.help:
**Channel mapping**: rovers use the *roll* channel for steering (RCMAP_ROLL, default 1) and *throttle* for speed (RCMAP_THROTTLE, default 3). Apply the mapping first, then calibrate.

**Calibration** records min/max of all channels while you move the sticks, the centre trim, and detects reversed channels from stick directions.

**Steering input type**: *Two paddles* if you drive a skid-steer vehicle with two sticks/paddles (left/right).

**Flight modes**: MODE_CH is the switch channel; MODE1..6 are the six switch positions. Recommended: Manual, Acro, Hold and Guided/Auto/RTL somewhere for later.

**Switch functions**: each RC channel that isn't steering, throttle or the mode switch can trigger a function with a transmitter switch (RCx_OPTION) - e.g. RTL, Hold, save waypoint, arm/disarm, relays, the gripper or a Lua script.

Steering, throttle and the mode switch must be three different channels (Apply refuses otherwise). A switch function left on one of those channels would fire with the stick or the mode switch (and on the mode channel ArduPilot refuses to arm), so Apply removes it and says so.

If a stick doesn't move its mapped channel during *Calibrate radio*, the wizard doesn't guess its direction: it names the channel that moved instead - set that as the steering/throttle channel, Apply, and calibrate again.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-radio-control-calibration.html>

wheel_encoders.help:
Wheel encoders improve speed and position estimates (especially with poor GPS). Configure type, pins and counts per revolution, **reboot**, then roll the vehicle by hand over a measured distance with *Calibrate radius*; the wizard corrects the wheel radius from the ratio *measured / reported* distance. If the distance goes **down** when rolling forward swap the A/B pins. The EKF must also be told to use the encoders: set *Horizontal velocity from* = Wheel encoders on the **Position sources** step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>

gimbal.intro: Set up one or two camera gimbals (mounts) so they can be pointed from the ground station or a mission.
gimbal.help:
**Number of gimbals**: ArduPilot supports two; with two, choose which one to configure.

**Gimbal type**: *Servo* / *Brushless PWM* gimbals use servo outputs (assign SERVOx_FUNCTION for mount tilt/pan/roll); serial gimbals (Siyi, SToRM32 serial, Viewpro) and MAVLink gimbals (Gremsy, SToRM32 MAVLink) need the **serial port** they are wired to - the wizard sets its protocol on Apply.

**Probe** tries the serial and MAVLink gimbal types on the chosen port, at the port's current baud rate first and then at other common rates, rebooting after each; after each reboot the gimbal is told to tilt down and you say whether it moved.

**Limits**: how far the gimbal may pitch and yaw. *Test gimbal* tilts it down and back.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-cameras-and-gimbals.html>

servo_outputs.intro: Set up extra devices on free servo outputs (PWM-controlled lights, additional servos etc.) and choose what drives them.
servo_outputs.help:
**Outputs** lists every servo output and its current job. Outputs used by the steering, the motors, a gimbal or anything else are shown but can't be changed here.

**Output to configure**: pick an output; the fields below then show its settings. *+*/*-* next to it move the output a step (the vehicle stays disarmed).

**Driven by**: *Follows RC channel k* passes an RC channel (a knob, slider or switch on your transmitter) straight to the output - the usual way to dim PWM lights or move an extra servo. *RC pass-through* uses the RC channel with the same number as the output. *GPIO pin* turns the output into a digital pin for a relay (set it up on the Relays step). *Not used*: missions and ground stations can still move it with DO_SET_SERVO.

**MIN/MAX/TRIM/Reverse**: end points, centre and direction of the output. A change of *Driven by* needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-servo.html>

relays.intro: Set up relays - digital on/off outputs and the RC switch that toggles them.
relays.help:
A **relay** in ArduPilot is a digital output pin switched between 0 V and 3.3/5 V; drive a real relay module or a MOSFET board from it (the pin itself supplies very little current).

**Relay to configure**: pick relay 1-6; *On*/*Off* switch it for a test. **Function**: *Relay* (firmware 4.5 and later). **GPIO pin number**: the board's number for the pin (see below). **Servo output used as this pin**: if the pin is a servo output, the wizard sets that output's SERVOx_FUNCTION to GPIO (-1).

**State at start-up** and **Inverted** (ON = low level) decide what the pin does at boot and when on. **Switched by RC channel**: a transmitter switch on that channel toggles the relay (RCx_OPTION); it must not be a channel used for steering, throttle or the mode switch.

Pin and function changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-relay.html>

gripper.intro: Set up a gripper - a servo or electro-permanent magnet - for deliveries and drops.
gripper.help:
**Gripper enabled**, then **type** (the other settings appear after Apply). A *servo* gripper needs its **servo output** (set to the Gripper function) and the pulse widths for **grab**, **release** and **neutral**. *Close again after release* re-grabs after that many seconds (0 = stay open).

**Operated by RC channel**: a transmitter switch opens/closes the gripper (RCx_OPTION = Gripper). *Test: grab*/*Test: release* try it; missions use DO_GRIPPER. Type changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-gripper-landingpage.html>

temperature.intro: Set up I2C or analog temperature sensors.
temperature.help:
Pick a sensor, then its **type**, the **I2C bus** (0-3) and the sensor's **I2C address** (decimal - e.g. 90 for an MLX90614). Sensors of the same type need different addresses. **Logging** decides which temperature reports are written to the log. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-temperature-sensor.html>

sprayer.intro: Set up a crop sprayer (pump and optional spinner) whose rate follows the vehicle's speed.
sprayer.help:
**Sprayer enabled** first (the other settings are read after Apply). The **pump** and optional **spinner** outputs get the SprayerPump/SprayerSpinner functions. **Pump rate at 1 m/s**: pump output in percent at 1 m/s - it scales with speed. **Minimum pump rate** keeps the pump running when slow; **Start spraying above** a minimum speed. **Spinner PWM** is the spinner's output when on.

Rover's RC switch functions don't include the sprayer, so there is no transmitter switch for it here.

optical_flow.intro: Set up an optical flow sensor for ground-speed measurement without GPS.
optical_flow.help:
**Sensor type**: I2C (PX4Flow, Pixart ...), MAVLink, DroneCAN or MSP (MSP sensors also need their serial port set to MSP on the Serial ports step). **Scale corrections** fine-tune the measured speed (parts per thousand); **mounting yaw** compensates a rotated sensor; **position** is its place on the vehicle. The sensor needs a rangefinder pointing down to scale its readings.

To actually use it, choose *Optical flow* as the horizontal velocity source on the **Position sources** step. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-optical-flow-sensor-setup.html>

visual_odometry.intro: Set up a tracking camera or companion computer that sends position estimates.
visual_odometry.help:
**Type**: *MAVLink* for a companion computer sending vision position messages, *Intel T265* or *VOXL* for those cameras (connected via a companion computer on a MAVLink serial port). **Camera position**: where the camera sits relative to the vehicle's centre.

To use it, choose *ExternalNav* on the **Position sources** step. An RC switch set to *Visual odometry yaw align* re-aligns the camera's heading. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-non-gps-navigation-landing-page.html>

beacon.intro: Set up local positioning beacons for navigation without GPS.
beacon.help:
**Beacon system**: Pozyx, Marvelmind or Nooploop; the receiver is connected to a **serial port** (set to the Beacon protocol at 115200 baud on Apply). **Origin latitude/longitude/altitude**: roughly where the beacons are - close enough for the magnetic declination lookup.

To use them, choose *Beacon* for horizontal (and optionally vertical) position on the **Position sources** step. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-non-gps-navigation-landing-page.html>

ekf_sources.intro: Tell the EKF (extended kalman filter) which sensors provide position, velocity and heading - up to three source sets, switchable during operation.
ekf_sources.help:
ArduPilot's EKF (EKF3) estimates where the vehicle is, how fast it moves and where it points, from the sources chosen here. The default (source set 1): horizontal position and velocity from GPS, vertical position from the barometer, vertical velocity from GPS, heading from the compass - right for a vehicle with GPS and compass.

**Heading from**: *Compass* is the default. Without a compass choose the *GSF estimator* (it works out the heading from GPS velocity and the IMU once the vehicle drives); with a dual-antenna (moving baseline) GPS choose *GPS, compass as fallback* (or *GPS*). The wizard proposes these when they fit.

**Vertical position from**: *GPS* instead of the barometer is an option with an accurate (RTK) GPS; a rover rarely needs altitude, but it is logged and shown.

Without GPS: *Beacon* or *ExternalNav* (visual odometry) for position, *Optical flow*, *ExternalNav* or *Wheel encoders* for velocity.

**Source sets**: up to three sets (EK3_SRC1_* to EK3_SRC3_*) - e.g. set 1 GPS for outdoors, set 2 beacons or visual odometry for indoors. Pick a set to configure it. An RC switch changes between them in operation, or *Use this source set now* switches immediately (apply first). Source changes need a **reboot**.

**Estimator**: standard firmware since 4.5 only contains EKF3 (EKF2 is compiled out and will be removed), so it must be selected and enabled. The EKF runs one instance per IMU ticked here.

**Sensor settings** (shown for the sensors the vehicle has): how much the EKF trusts wheel encoders and visual odometry, and the measurement delays of optical flow and beacons.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-ekf-sources.html>

osd.intro: Set up an on-screen display that overlays flight data on the FPV video.
osd.help:
**OSD type**: *MAX7456* for a board's built-in analog OSD; *MSP* or *MSP DisplayPort* for digital systems (DJI, HDZero, Walksnail ...) - their serial port must be set to MSP or DisplayPort on the Serial ports step. **Screen switched by RC channel** changes between up to four screen layouts. **Units**, **font** and warning levels apply to all screens. Screen layouts (item positions) are edited best in a ground station's OSD editor. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-osd-overview.html>

remote_id.intro: Set up a Remote ID (OpenDroneID) transmitter module.
remote_id.help:
Remote ID needs firmware built with OpenDroneID support (e.g. from custom.ardupilot.org, category Ident) - on standard firmware these settings don't exist and the step says so.

The module is connected either to a **serial port** (MAVLink - the wizard sets the port to MAVLink2 if it is unused) or to **DroneCAN**. **Options**: enforce the Remote ID arming checks, no emergency status when driving without GPS, lock the UAS ID. Operator and UAS IDs are entered in a ground station's Remote ID panel. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-remoteid.html>

rpm.intro: Set up RPM sensors - engine, wheel or motor RPM from ESC telemetry.
rpm.help:
Up to four sensors. **GPIO pin**: a hall-effect or optical sensor on a digital pin; if the pin is a servo output, choose it and the wizard switches that output to GPIO. **Scaling** converts pulses to RPM (see its help). **ESC telemetry** averages the RPM of the ESCs in the bitmask. **Harmonic notch** reports the notch filter's frequency. **Min/max RPM** and **minimum quality** reject implausible readings.

*Show RPM* lists the live readings of sensors 1 and 2. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rpm.html>

generator.intro: Set up a generator or fuel cell that reports over a serial port.
generator.help:
**Generator type** and the **serial port** it is connected to (set to the Generator protocol with the chosen baud rate on Apply). **Options**: the one option ArduPilot documents suppresses maintenance-required warnings. To monitor its output, set a second battery monitor to *Generator (electrical)* (BATTx_MONITOR = 17) or *Generator (fuel)* (18) with a ground station. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-generators.html>

serial_ports.intro: Choose what each serial port is used for, and its baud rate.
serial_ports.help:
**Serial ports** lists every port's protocol and baud rate. Pick a port to change it. Other steps (GPS, rangefinder, proximity sensor, gimbal) set their ports themselves; this step is for everything else - telemetry radios (MAVLink2), RC receivers on a UART (RC input), ESC telemetry, and so on.

**Careful**: changing the port the wizard is connected through (e.g. a telemetry radio) ends the connection after the reboot. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-serial-options.html>

battery.intro: Configure the battery monitor, calibrate voltage/current and set low-battery actions.
battery.help:
**BATT_MONITOR** selects the sensor type (analog power module, SMBus, DroneCAN...). For analog sensors calibrate with a multimeter: enter the real pack voltage, press *Calibrate voltage*, then *Apply*. The same works for current with a clamp meter under load. Changing the monitor type requires a reboot.

**Failsafes**: the *low* / *critical* action starts when the voltage stays below *Low voltage* / *Critical voltage* for longer than *Below the voltage for* (BATT_LOW_TIMER, default 10 s), so a short dip while accelerating doesn't count. *Sag-compensated* voltage estimates the resting voltage and reacts even less to load. *Low / Critical remaining capacity* start the same actions on the capacity left (needs a current sensor; 0 = off). Critical must be below low. **Battery capacity** itself only sets the percentage shown - it doesn't trigger anything.

**The percentage is counted from the current used since the flight controller started** (except smart batteries): after every boot it starts at 100 %, even with a half-empty pack. *Minimum voltage to arm* (BATT_ARM_VOLT) refuses to arm on a pack that is already low.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-power-module-configuration-in-mission-planner.html>

failsafe.intro: Decide what the vehicle does upon failure and set arming rules.
failsafe.help:
* **FS_ACTION**: what to do on failsafe (Hold is a good default for testing, RTL/SmartRTL for autonomous work).
* **Throttle failsafe** triggers when the throttle PWM falls below FS_THR_VALUE or the radio signal is lost.
* **GCS failsafe**: triggered when telemetry heartbeats stop for the timeout.
* **Crash check**: detects when the vehicle stops moving during Auto.
* **ARMING_CHECK**: leave on *All* unless you know why not.

**Arming checks**: every ticked check must pass before the vehicle arms. Untick a check only for bench testing or when its hardware isn't fitted - a failed check usually means something needs fixing. (Firmware before 4.7 stores this in ARMING_CHECK, later in ARMING_SKIPCHK; the wizard handles both.)

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-failsafes.html>

scripting.intro: Enable scripting and set up the scripting engine.
scripting.help:
**Scripting**: enables the Lua engine. After enabling, **reboot** - then the other settings appear here and the APM/scripts folder is created on the SD card; copy .lua files there.

**Memory for scripts**: raise it if the flight controller reports 'Scripting: out of memory'. **Script folders**: run scripts built into the firmware (ROMFS) and/or from the SD card. **Debug** options add messages and logs. **User parameters** 1-6 are free values scripts can read.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>

save.intro:
Review what was changed and reboot the flight controller so all settings take effect.

You can also revert all previously applied changes.
save.help:
Some parameters (output functions, frame, PWM type, encoders, battery monitor, GPS type, calibrations) only take effect after a **reboot**. Do it now, then come back for **Phase 2** - which needs the vehicle armed outdoors. The list of changes is kept so you can *revert everything* if needed. A parameter backup (**Ctrl+P**, **Backup**) keeps the finished Phase 1 setup in a file.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/apmrover-setup.html>

predrive.intro: Check GPS/EKF/RC/battery and enter the free space around the vehicle's START position. ARM the vehicle outdoors before continuing.
predrive.help:
**Everything from here on drives the vehicle.** Go outdoors, choose an open, flat area, put the vehicle on the ground, and **arm** it with the Arm button (or your transmitter).

**Where the distances are measured from:** every automatic run starts where the vehicle stands at that moment (its *start point*), and the distances below are measured from there:

* **Straight runway** - the free distance straight ahead of the vehicle's nose. Straight runs go forward only.
* **Circle** - all automatic turns go to the **right**. The free circle lies beside the vehicle: the vehicle stands on its edge, facing along it, with the circle's centre to its right (half the diameter away).

```
     .-~~~~~-.
   /           \
  ^      +      |
   \           /
     '-.___.-'

^ vehicle on the edge, facing up
+ centre, half the diameter to its right
```

The automatic stop measures the straight-line distance from the start point (from GPS/EKF position; without one, the distance travelled) and ends the run at the limit. It can't tell a planned circle from a drift sideways, so the circle is the area to keep clear, not a fence. Put the vehicle back at a start point with enough free space before each run.

It uses RC override in Manual mode (open-loop tests) and Guided mode (closed-loop tests); if the wizard or the link dies, the override expires after ~3 s and the transmitter/failsafe takes over. The **STOP** button releases all commands, switches to Hold and disarms.

The RC failsafe test verifies that switching the transmitter off really stops the vehicle.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>

direction_check.intro: A first slow drive: forward must be forward, right must be right.
direction_check.help:
The vehicle creeps forward and then steers right. The wizard compares the commanded direction with the measured speed and yaw rate. If something is inverted it offers to fix it (toggle *reversed* on the motor/steering output, or swap left/right on skid-steer vehicles).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>

top_speed.help:
**SPEED_MAX** is the speed at full throttle - the vehicle accelerates in a straight line at 100% throttle until the speed is constant. From the same run the maximum **acceleration** (ATC_ACCEL_MAX) and **deceleration** (ATC_DECEL_MAX, 0 = same as acceleration) are derived with a safety factor of 0.9. If your runway is too short the speed is still rising: the result is only a lower bound - repeat with a longer runway.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-throttle-and-speed.html>

turning.intro: Measure TURN_RADIUS, the maximum turn rate and steering acceleration.
turning.help:
**Radius**: drives a full-lock circle at low speed and computes radius = speed / yaw rate. **Max turn rate**: the peak yaw rate with full steering (pivot for skid-steer, medium speed for front-wheel steering). It is multiplied by 0.9 and written to **ACRO_TURN_RATE** and **ATC_STR_RAT_MAX**; the steepest yaw-rate slope gives **ATC_STR_ACC_MAX**. Skid-steer vehicles can pivot: also review the pivot parameters in the *Navigation* step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-steering-rate.html>

gains.intro: Calculate steering-rate and speed feed-forward, cruise speed/throttle and starting P/I gains.
gains.help:
Uses the same maths as ArduPilot's **QuickTune** script: *steering FF* = steering output / measured yaw rate; *speed*: CRUISE_SPEED and CRUISE_THROTTLE are the steady speed and throttle at a medium throttle level, and the speed P and I start at throttle-per-(m/s). Steering P = I = 0.5 x FF. Filters are set to half the gyro filter. Run these tests on flat, dry ground you will normally drive on. Optionally assign a transmitter switch to ArduPilot's **QuickTune** script for later fine-tuning while driving (see the switch field's ❓; scripting itself is enabled on the **Scripting** step).

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/PIDReview> to review PID tune from logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-process.html>

verify.intro: Let the controllers follow speed and turn-rate steps and refine P/I automatically.
verify.help:
In Guided mode the vehicle follows a **speed step** and a **yaw-rate step**. Overshoot, rise time and steady-state error are measured; P and I are corrected (overshoot -> lower P/I, slow -> raise P, steady error -> raise I) and the test is repeated up to the chosen number of rounds. In *manual* mode you drive in Acro and get achieved/desired ratios (edit the values yourself). Vehicle needs a position estimate (GPS or wheel encoders) for Guided mode.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/PIDReview> to review PID tune from logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-process.html>

navigation.intro: Mission speed, waypoint radius and (for skid steering) pivot-turn behaviour.
navigation.help:
**WP_SPEED** is the default mission speed (cruise speed is a good value). **WP_RADIUS** is how close the vehicle must get to a waypoint to count it reached (about the turn radius or larger). **NAVL1_PERIOD** is the path-tracking aggressiveness - larger is smoother, smaller follows the line more tightly. Skid-steer vehicles pivot on the spot when the heading error exceeds the pivot angle. Test in Auto with a small square mission afterwards and adjust.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-tuning-navigation.html>

log_settings.intro: Choose where the flight controller logs, what it logs, and when.
log_settings.help:
**Log to SD card file** is the usual choice; MAVLink streaming needs a receiver on the other end. **Log** items choose the content - more items give more insight but bigger files. **Log while disarmed** helps to diagnose problems before arming (*except on USB power* keeps bench sessions out of the logs); a **rate limit** keeps those logs small. **New log file after each disarm** splits the logs per drive.

Also don't miss <https://firmware.ardupilot.org/Tools/WebTools/LogFinder> to load/sort log directories and <https://plot.ardupilot.org/#/> to view logs in your browser.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>

final.intro: Final review of all changes; disarm.
final.help:
Review the list of changed parameters, save a parameter backup (**Ctrl+P**, **Backup**) and keep the file somewhere safe as the record of the finished setup. **Next steps**: fly a small Auto mission square, watch the tracking in your ground station, and lower WP_SPEED / raise NAVL1_PERIOD if the vehicle oscillates. Re-run *Verify* after changing tyres, payload or battery.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/apmrover-setup.html>

distance_sensors.intro: Set up rangefinders and proximity sensors, and ArduPilot's object avoidance.
distance_sensors.help:
**Rangefinders** measure one distance in one fixed direction - forward for obstacle detection, down as a boat's echosounder. **Proximity sensors** report distances in several directions around the vehicle (e.g. a 360-degree lidar); object avoidance uses them. The proximity type **RangeFinder** connects the two: it feeds every rangefinder pointing horizontally (forward, sideways or back) into object avoidance.

**Rangefinders** (up to 10): pick one to configure. **Type** is the driver ArduPilot uses; I2C sensors also need their **I2C address**, serial sensors the **serial port** they are wired to (set to the Rangefinder protocol at 115200 baud on Apply). **Probe** tries the common I2C sensors (LightWare, Benewake, VL53L0X/L1X, Maxbotix) and, with a serial port chosen, the LightWare and Benewake serial drivers at the port's current baud rate and then at other common rates - rebooting after each - until one reports a distance; point the sensor at something 0.5-3 m away first. **Min/max distance**: what the sensor reads reliably (older firmware uses centimetres).

**Proximity sensors** (up to 5): pick one to configure. Serial sensors (RPLidar, LightWare SF40/C and SF45B, TeraRanger Tower, Cygbot, LD06) need their **serial port** - set to the Lidar360 protocol with the chosen **baud rate** on Apply (RPLidar A2 115200, S1/A2M12 256000, C1 460800, SF40/C 921600). **Probe** tries RPLidar and SF40/C on the chosen port - at the port's current baud rate, their usual rates, then other common rates - until the sensor reports distances in several directions. **Mounting**: on top, or upside down underneath.

**Object avoidance**: tick *proximity sensors* so the rover keeps the **margin** from obstacles; **behaviour** decides whether it slides along or stops. *Show distances* lists the live readings. Type and port changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rangefinder-landingpage.html>

sails.intro: Set up the sail actuator and how ArduPilot trims the sail.
sails.help:
**The sail is moved by** one kind of actuator (`SERVOx_FUNCTION`): a *sail winch* pulling the main sheet (89), a *wing sail elevator* turning a free wing (128), or a *servo turning the mast* (137). Assign its output and press Apply. *Test -* / *Test +* move it to either end with ArduPilot's sail motor test (it **arms** the vehicle for 3 s). A winch at *-* must pull the sail **in**; if it lets it out, tick **Reverse output**. Set MIN/MAX so the boom comes in to the centre line without being pulled down hard, and goes out to the shrouds (about 90 deg).

**Boom angles** (winch only): the angle between the centre line and the boom at each end, so ArduPilot knows the sail angle in between. **Ideal angle**: the angle the sail keeps to the apparent wind - raise it if the sail is too loose. Check it in Acro.

**Heel**: above *Maximum heel angle* a PID controller lets the sail out (it never pulls it in). Mostly P and I; D is too fast for a sail winch.

**Sailing**: upwind ArduPilot sails at the *closest angle to the wind* and tacks when it reaches the *cross-track error*. A **tack switch** tacks in Acro and Auto. In Manual the throttle stick moves the sail (stick down = in) - with a motor, the motor too, unless the sail gets an RC channel of its own; a three-position switch chooses the motor: never / below the minimum wind speed / always.

Settings appear after `SAIL_ENABLE` is set and the flight controller rebooted. Tune steering and navigation as usual afterwards - on all points of sail.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>

wind_vane.intro: Tell ArduPilot where the wind comes from - and how strong it is.
wind_vane.help:
Sailing relies on the **apparent wind** - the wind the vehicle feels. ArduPilot gets its direction from **Wind direction from** and, optionally, its speed from **Wind speed from**; it works out the true wind from them and the vehicle's own speed.

Without a sensor ArduPilot can assume the wind comes from where the vehicle pointed when it was armed (optionally offset by an RC knob) - only for first tests.

**Analog vane** (a potentiometer): set the input pin, then *Calibrate direction*: turn the vane round for 30 s while the flight controller records the voltage range. Turning it clockwise must raise the voltage. **NMEA 0183 sensor** (e.g. an ultrasonic anemometer): choose its serial port and baud rate (an RS-422/RS-232 converter is needed). For both, *Set headwind offset* with the vane pointing at the bow.

**Wind speed**: a wind speed sensor isn't required, but helps, the faster the vehicle sails. The Modern Devices sensor needs *Calibrate zero wind speed* while sheltered from the wind.

Mount the sensors as high as possible, in clear air. Type changes need a **reboot**; the other settings appear after it.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>

torqeedo.intro: Connect a Torqeedo electric outboard over its RS485 bus.
torqeedo.help:
ArduPilot drives a Torqeedo Travel, Ultralight or Cruise through an **RS485-to-serial converter**, at 19200 baud; the motor follows the throttle output. **Connected to**: the *tiller connector* of the Torqeedo battery, or the *motor connector* (with another battery - use one with short-circuit protection).

Choose the serial port; Apply sets it to the Torqeedo protocol (39) at 19200 baud. A port with flow-control pins (RTS/CTS) needs nothing more; otherwise wire the **on/off** and **driver-enable** pins to AUX pins.

The battery monitor can read voltage and current from the Torqeedo (`BATT_MONITOR` = 23). Settings appear after the type is set and the flight controller rebooted. Until the motor answers, arming reports *Torqeedo: not healthy*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>

depth_sounder.intro: Set up an echosounder to measure the water depth.
depth_sounder.help:
An echosounder is a **rangefinder pointing down**: Apply sets its orientation to *Down* (25). ArduPilot then logs the depth with the position (DPTH) and sends it to the ground station (WATER_DEPTH) - e.g. for mapping the bottom.

Pick your **echosounder** and press *Fill in*: type, baud rate and range from its page in ArduPilot's documentation (most speak NMEA 0183 at the baud rate set in the sounder). Choose the serial port; Apply sets it to the Rangefinder protocol (9).

The transducer must be under water to measure. Type changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>

boat_loiter.intro: How the boat holds its position in Loiter mode and at the end of a route.
boat_loiter.help:
A boat can't stop: wind and current carry it away. In **Loiter** - and wherever Auto, Guided, RTL and SmartRTL arrive - it drifts while it is within the **radius** of its target and drives back once it is further away, at (distance beyond the radius) x the **speed gain**, at most WP_SPEED.

**Way back**: either direction (least turning, unpredictable heading), always bow first (e.g. a camera at the bow), or always stern first (bow into the current).

**After the last mission item**: boats loiter by default. For good position holding the ESC dead-band must be small (`MOT_THR_MIN`, Motor output step). A sailing boat uses `SAIL_LOIT_RADIUS` while it sails.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/loiter-mode.html>

fields.vehicle_type.vehicle_info:
Firmware version, MAVLink ids and which SERVO outputs are already assigned to steering/throttle - queried automatically whenever this step is opened.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/apmrover-setup.html>
fields.vehicle_type.heavy_vehicle:
Enables **Large Vehicle MagCal** on the Compass calibration step: enter a known heading instead of rotating the vehicle by hand.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-calibration-in-mission-planner.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_gps:
Needed for position-based modes (Auto, Guided, RTL, Loiter) and the navigation step. Without GPS the GPS step is hidden and GPS_TYPE is set to None.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-positioning-landing-page.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_compass:
Unchecked: COMPASS_ENABLE = 0 and the compass step is hidden. Compass-less operation needs a GPS (the EKF estimates the heading from GPS movement) or GPS-for-yaw.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compassless.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_rc:
Unchecked: RC calibration, the RC failsafe settings and the RC failsafe test are hidden. You then drive from a ground station/joystick - set up the GCS failsafe, and check that ARMING_CHECK does not require RC. Detected from the receiver's signal (there is no parameter for it): switch the transmitter on before connecting, or tick the box yourself.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rc-systems.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_battery_monitor:
A power module / voltage sensor. Unchecked: BATT_MONITOR = 0, battery step and battery failsafe hidden.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-power-module-configuration-in-mission-planner.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_wenc:
Enables the Wheel encoders step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_rangefinder:
A single-direction lidar/sonar, e.g. for obstacle detection or a boat's echosounder.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rangefinder-landingpage.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_proximity:
A sensor measuring distances in several directions around the vehicle - e.g. a 360-degree lidar such as RPLidar or LightWare SF40/C - used for object avoidance.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-proximity-landingpage.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_gimbal:
One or two stabilised or servo camera mounts.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-cameras-and-gimbals.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_aux_servos:
PWM-controlled lights, extra servos and similar on free servo outputs, usually driven by an RC knob or switch. Enables the Servo outputs step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-servo.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_relays:
Switched lights, horns, pumps ... on a relay (a digital output pin). Enables the Relays step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-relay.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_gripper:
A servo or electro-permanent-magnet gripper, e.g. for deliveries.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-gripper-landingpage.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_temperature:
I2C or analog temperature sensors (TEMPn_ parameters, firmware 4.3 and later).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-temperature-sensor.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_sprayer: A crop sprayer: pump (and optional spinner) whose rate follows the speed.
fields.vehicle_type.has_optical_flow:
A downward camera measuring ground speed - for navigation without GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-optical-flow-sensors-landingpage.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_visual_odometry:
A tracking camera or companion computer sending position estimates (e.g. Intel T265, VOXL).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-non-gps-navigation-landing-page.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_beacons:
Indoor/local positioning beacons (Pozyx, Marvelmind, Nooploop).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-non-gps-navigation-landing-page.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_osd:
Flight data overlaid on the FPV video (onboard, MSP or DisplayPort OSD).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-osd-overview.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_remote_id:
An OpenDroneID transmitter. Needs firmware built with Remote ID support (custom.ardupilot.org).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-remoteid.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_rpm:
Engine or wheel RPM from a hall-effect/optical sensor, or motor RPM from ESC telemetry.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-rpm.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_generator:
A supported generator or fuel cell reporting over a serial port.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-generators.html>
fields.steering_output.rev_steering:
Use *Test L* / *Test R* above: if the wheels steer the other way, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.min_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse at full **left** lock: as far as the steering goes without binding. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (vehicle disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.max_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse at full **right** lock: as far as the steering goes without binding. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (vehicle disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.trim_steering:
Steering servo: the pulse that points the wheels straight ahead. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the servo there (vehicle disarmed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.MOT_PWM_FREQ:
Frequency for brushed drivers (parameter unit is kHz on recent firmware; see docs of your driver).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_throttle:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the motor turns its wheels backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.min_throttle:
ESC pulse for full reverse (or zero for an ESC that only drives forward). Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.max_throttle:
ESC pulse for full forward. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.trim_throttle:
ESC pulse for stop - the ESC's neutral. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_left:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the LEFT motor turns its wheels backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.min_left:
ESC pulse for full reverse (or zero for an ESC that only drives forward). Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.max_left:
ESC pulse for full forward. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.trim_left:
ESC pulse for stop - the ESC's neutral. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.rev_right:
Use the *Test* buttons above: if the RIGHT motor turns its wheels backwards on *Test ↑*, tick this box.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.min_right:
ESC pulse for full reverse (or zero for an ESC that only drives forward). Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.max_right:
ESC pulse for full forward. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.trim_right:
ESC pulse for stop - the ESC's neutral. Keep 1000 / 2000 / 1500 us unless your ESC is calibrated to other values - and calibrate the ESC to the same values. The motor isn't driven by *+* / *-*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.MOT_STR_THR_MIX:
0 = throttle has priority, 1 = steering has priority when the sum exceeds 100%.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.gps.gps_port:
The serial port the receiver is wired to (SERIALx_PROTOCOL is set to GPS). ArduPilot uses the lowest-numbered GPS port for GPS 1, so GPS 1 must be on a lower port than GPS 2. Choose 'Not on a serial port' for DroneCAN receivers.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-positioning-landing-page.html>
fields.compass.COMPASS_AUTO_ROT:
During the rotate-by-hand calibration ArduPilot can detect (and fix) how an external compass is mounted. 'Check and fix' is the usual choice; use the 45-degree variant for compasses mounted at 45 degrees.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-calibration-in-mission-planner.html>
fields.compass.magcal_heading:
0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west. Get this from a phone compass app (set to true-north mode if it offers one) or by sighting a known landmark bearing - accuracy here directly limits the calibration's accuracy.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-calibration-in-mission-planner.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC_TYPE:
Quadrature encoders need two GPIO pins (A/B). Reboot required after changing the type.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC_CPR:
Encoder counts per WHEEL revolution as seen by the autopilot (pulses x 4 for quadrature, x gear ratio).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC_RADIUS:
Rolling radius. Use the calibration button below to refine it precisely.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC_POS_X:
Position relative to the vehicle's centre of gravity/IMU.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC_PINA:
Board specific GPIO number of channel A (see BRD_PWM_COUNT / AUX pin numbers in the docs).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>

Quadrature encoders need two GPIO pins (A/B). Reboot required after changing the type.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>

Encoder counts per WHEEL revolution as seen by the autopilot (pulses x 4 for quadrature, x gear ratio).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>

Rolling radius. Use the calibration button below to refine it precisely.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wheel-encoder.html>
fields.wheel_encoders.WENC2_POS_X:
Position relative to the vehicle's centre of gravity/IMU.

**QuickTune** is ArduPilot's Lua script `rover-quicktune.lua` (from ArduPilot's `AP_Scripting/applets`). It refines the same gains as this step - steering FF/P/I/D, the steering filters, cruise speed and throttle, speed P/I/D - while the rover drives circles, and is controlled by a transmitter switch. Enter the RC channel of a 2- or 3-position switch (not steering, throttle or the mode channel); Apply gives it the script's switch function (`RCx_OPTION` = 300, or the script's `RTUN_RC_FUNC` if you changed it).

**Before it works:**

1. Enable Lua scripting on the **Scripting** step, then reboot.
2. Copy `rover-quicktune.lua` into `APM/scripts` on the flight controller's SD card, then reboot again - its `RTUN_` parameters then appear in the parameter list (Ctrl+P).

**Using it:** arm, switch to **Circle** mode (optionally set `CIRC_SPEED` to about half the top speed and `CIRC_RADIUS` to at least twice the turn radius). Switch **middle** = start tuning (progress messages appear in the log); after *RTUN: tuning done*, switch **high** = save. Switch **low** before saving, or disarming, reverts the gains. Steering or throttle input pauses tuning for a few seconds.
