fields.predrive.runway:
The free, flat distance **straight ahead of the vehicle's nose**, measured from where it stands when a run starts. Straight runs use part of it and stop automatically once the vehicle is that far from its start point: the direction check at most 20 % (at least 3 m), top speed and cruise runs at most 60 % (the rest is for stopping), the speed-controller step up to 90 %.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>
fields.predrive.circle_d:
Diameter of the free circle for the turning runs. All automatic turns go to the **right**: the vehicle stands on the circle's edge, facing along it, with the centre half the diameter to its right. Turning runs (turn radius, max turn rate, steering feed-forward, steering-rate step) stop automatically once the vehicle is this far (straight line) from its start point. A full-lock circle needs a diameter of at least twice the turn radius.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-first-drive.html>
fields.motor_output.esc_dir:
What your ESC / motor driver does below neutral:

* **Forward and reverse** - drives backwards (most rover ESCs, H-bridges, *brushed with relay*).
* **Forward and brake** - a car ESC that brakes first (and reverses only after a pause at neutral).
* **Forward only** - no reverse, no brake (e.g. many boat or aircraft ESCs).

**Forward only** sets the motor outputs' TRIM to their MIN, so zero throttle is the lowest pulse instead of the middle, and switches the speed controller's braking (`ATC_BRAKE`) off. Switching back to a reversible ESC puts TRIM in the middle of the range - check the ESC's neutral with the TRIM button on the *Servo outputs* step.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.ATC_BRAKE:
Whether the **speed controller** (Acro, Guided, Auto, RTL ...) may send *reverse* throttle to slow down. **Yes** stops faster and holds speed better downhill; **No** only lets the vehicle coast.

Reverse output while still rolling forward loads the gears: with a geared drive and an ESC without a brake, choose **No**, or protect it with *Pause before changing direction* and a moderate *Throttle slew rate*. Manual mode isn't affected (there the stick decides). Not shown for forward-only ESCs (always off).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.motor_output.MOT_REV_DELAY:
`MOT_REV_DELAY`: when the motor's direction changes, the output stays at zero for this long before the new direction is driven - in every mode, Manual included. Protects gearboxes and ESCs that can't reverse instantly. **0 = off** (ArduPilot's default); 0.1 .. 1 s otherwise, e.g. 0.3 s for a geared brushed motor.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-motor-and-servo-configuration.html>
fields.failsafe.fence_heading:
A **geofence** is a safety net that works without the wizard or the radio link: when the vehicle crosses it while armed - in *any* mode, Manual included - ArduPilot switches to the mode chosen under *When crossed*. More than 100 m outside the fence it always switches to Hold.

The circle is centred on **home** (where the vehicle was armed), so it needs a position (GPS): with the fence on, arming waits for one.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-geofencing-landing-page.html>
fields.failsafe.FENCE_ENABLE:
Switches the geofence on. Recommended for the first drives in Phase 2.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-geofencing-landing-page.html>
fields.failsafe.fence_circle:
A circle of the radius below around home (where the vehicle was armed).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-ac2_simple_geofence.html>
fields.failsafe.fence_zones:
Inclusion / exclusion circles and polygons you upload with a ground station (e.g. Mission Planner's *Geo-Fence*). Without uploaded zones this has no effect.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-polygon_fence.html>
fields.failsafe.FENCE_RADIUS:
Radius of the circle around home, at least 30 m. For the first drives choose a little more than the free area you'll use - the runway length is a good start.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-geofencing-landing-page.html>
fields.failsafe.FENCE_ACTION:
What happens when the fence is crossed. **Hold** (stop) is the safest choice for the first drives; RTL needs a working navigation setup, which Phase 2 is still tuning.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-geofencing-landing-page.html>
fields.compass.COMPASS_MOTCT:
*Use current* subtracts the motor interference measured below, scaled with the battery current. *Use throttle* has no effect on a Rover (ArduPilot only feeds the throttle to the compass on Copter). The measurement proposes *Use current* together with the X/Y/Z values; Apply writes them.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.compassmot_power:
Highest motor power during the measurement. The motors run at a third, two thirds and all of it, each for about 4.5 s with motor-off pauses in between. More power means more current and a more reliable result - use as much as is safe with the wheels lifted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.mot_x:
Added to the first compass's X reading per amp of battery current (COMPASS_MOT_X, or COMPASS_MOT2_/MOT3_ when ArduPilot uses another compass first). Normally set by the measurement, not by hand.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.mot_y:
Added to the first compass's Y reading per amp of battery current (COMPASS_MOT_Y, or COMPASS_MOT2_/MOT3_ when ArduPilot uses another compass first). Normally set by the measurement, not by hand.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.mot_z:
Added to the first compass's Z reading per amp of battery current (COMPASS_MOT_Z, or COMPASS_MOT2_/MOT3_ when ArduPilot uses another compass first). Normally set by the measurement, not by hand.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.COMPASS_DEC:
Angle between true north and magnetic north at your location in degrees, east positive (about +4 in central Germany, -13 in New York). Look it up with a magnetic declination calculator for your location. ArduPilot stores it in radians (COMPASS_DEC); the wizard converts.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.compass_list:
The compasses the flight controller found: internal (on the board) or external, and their priority - the one used first is the one ArduPilot navigates with.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.compass_use1:
Whether ArduPilot may use compass 1 for the heading (the COMPASS_USE parameter of its priority). Switch off an internal compass that is disturbed by motors when an external one is fitted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.compass_use2:
Whether ArduPilot may use compass 2 for the heading (the COMPASS_USE parameter of its priority). Switch off an internal compass that is disturbed by motors when an external one is fitted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.compass.compass_use3:
Whether ArduPilot may use compass 3 for the heading (the COMPASS_USE parameter of its priority). Switch off an internal compass that is disturbed by motors when an external one is fitted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-compass-setup-advanced.html>
fields.gps.gps_checks:
Before EKF3 starts using the GPS - and so before the vehicle may arm - the GPS has to pass every ticked check without interruption for 10 seconds (`EK3_GPS_CHECK`). A failing check is named in the log, e.g. *PreArm: GPS horiz error 6.1m (needs 5.0)*. The limits at an *Accepted GPS error* of 100 % (ArduPilot source, `AP_NavEKF3_VehicleStatus.cpp`):

* **Number of satellites**: at least 6
* **HDoP**: at most 2.5
* **Speed error**: the speed accuracy the GPS reports, at most 1.0 m/s
* **Position error**: the position accuracy the GPS reports, at most 5 m horizontally (7.5 m vertically)
* **Yaw error**: the compass heading agrees with the EKF
* **Position drift**: standing still, the position moves less than 3 m (a 0.3 m/s average drift or one 3 m jump)
* **Vertical speed / Horizontal speed**: standing still, the GPS speed stays below 0.3 m/s

**Accepted GPS error** (`EK3_CHECK_SCALE`, 50-200 %) scales all of these limits: 200 % doubles them. Once passed, the limits are 30 % wider so the result doesn't flicker.

ArduPilot's advice: all checks off is 0, all on is 255; 31 (the first five) is the strictest setting that still passes while the vehicle moves (e.g. starting from a boat).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.ekf_sources.ekf_estimator:
The Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) estimates the vehicle's position, velocity and orientation from the gyros, accelerometers, compass, GPS and barometer; by fusing all of them it can reject a single sensor's errors. Current ArduPilot uses EKF3 for this.

* **Estimator used** (`AHRS_EKF_TYPE`): 3 = EKF3. EKF2 lacks newer sources such as beacons, wheel encoders and visual odometry and is compiled out of standard firmware since 4.5 (`AP_AHRS_config.h`: slated to be removed).
* **EKF3** (`EK3_ENABLE`): makes the EKF3 maths run at all; it is only used for navigation with `AHRS_EKF_TYPE` = 3. Needs a reboot.
* **EKF instance for IMU n** (`EK3_IMU_MASK`): one EKF "core" runs per ticked IMU; at any time only the output of the core with the most consistent sensor data is used. ArduPilot's default runs cores on the first two IMUs (3). Each core needs memory and processor time - if there isn't enough, EKF3 fails to start.

Most vehicles need no changes here.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-apm-navigation-extended-kalman-filter-overview.html>
fields.ekf_sources.ekf_sensors:
How the EKF uses the extra sensors the vehicle has (shown only for those ticked on the Vehicle type step):

* **Wheel encoder speed error** (`EK3_WENC_VERR`): the 1-sigma speed error the EKF assumes for the wheel encoders. Smaller = the EKF trusts them more.
* **Optical flow delay** (`EK3_FLOW_DELAY`): how many milliseconds the flow measurements lag behind the IMU - from the end of the sensor's averaging period, not including its 100 ms of averaging.
* **Visual odometry speed error (min / max)** (`EK3_VIS_VERR_MIN` / `_MAX`): the 1-sigma speed error the EKF assumes when the camera reports its best / worst quality; between them it is interpolated linearly.
* **Beacon delay** (`EK3_BCN_DELAY`): how many milliseconds the beacon range measurements lag behind the IMU.

ArduPilot's defaults suit most sensors; change them only if the sensor's documentation says so.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-apm-navigation-extended-kalman-filter-overview.html>
fields.barometer.baro_list:
The barometers ArduPilot found at the last boot (`BARO1_DEVID` .. `BARO3_DEVID`): the sensor type and the bus it is on, decoded from the device ID. *used* marks the one ArduPilot takes its pressure from: the one chosen in `BARO_PRIMARY` (ArduPilot falls back to the first healthy one while it is unhealthy). A new external barometer appears here only after a reboot.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.barometer.baro_external:
Tick this if a barometer is connected to the flight controller's I2C port (or comes over MSP). ArduPilot only looks for the external sensor types ticked below (`BARO_PROBE_EXT`). Unticking it and pressing Apply sets `BARO_PROBE_EXT` to 0: no external barometer is looked for. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.barometer.baro_probe:
The sensor types ArduPilot looks for on the external I2C buses at boot (`BARO_PROBE_EXT`), each at its usual I2C address(es). Tick the type you connected. The *BMP388 / BMP390* and *SPL06 / SPA06* entries cover both chips; *MSP* is a barometer reported by an MSP device on a serial port, not an I2C sensor. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.barometer.BARO_EXT_BUS:
The I2C bus to search for the external barometer: -1 searches every external I2C bus (ArduPilot's list calls -1 *Disabled*, but the firmware then probes all external buses). Bus numbers are board-specific - leave -1 unless you know the bus. Changes need a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.log_settings.log_backend_1:
**SD card file**: logs are written as .BIN files to APM/LOGS on the SD card (on Linux boards: a directory). The usual choice - download them with a ground station or take the card out. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_backend_2:
**MAVLink**: the log is streamed over the MAVLink link and only exists if a ground station on the other end records it (e.g. MAVProxy, Mission Planner). Needs a fast, reliable link - over a telemetry radio parts of the log get lost. Can be ticked in addition to the SD card. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_backend_4:
**Onboard flash chip** (*Block*): for boards without an SD card that have a dataflash chip instead (and SITL). The chip is small, so old logs are erased early - keep *What to log* short. Download over MAVLink with a ground station. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_1:
**Fast attitude**: attitude (ATT), the EKF's own messages (XKF1..XKF5, XKQ ...), AHR2, POS and the steering and speed controllers' PID messages (PIDS, PIDA, and PIDW / PIDP / PIDR where used), written every main loop (`SCHED_LOOP_RATE`, 50 Hz by default). Needed to analyse tuning and EKF problems. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_2:
**Medium attitude**: the same messages as *Fast attitude* (ATT, XKF*, AHR2, POS, PID*), but at 10 Hz. Has no effect while *Fast attitude* is ticked. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_4:
**GPS**: every GPS's position, speed, satellites and accuracy (GPS, GPA) at the rate the GPS reports, plus the receiver's own messages for some types. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_8:
**System performance**: the main loop's timing and load, free memory and CPU use (PM) and the telemetry radio's signal and error counters (RAD) - shows whether the flight controller keeps up. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_16:
**Throttle**: throttle input and output, desired and actual speed and forward acceleration (THR) at 10 Hz - for tuning the speed controller; also beacon positions (BCN) when beacons are used. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_32:
**Navigation tuning**: distance and bearing to the waypoint, the bearing being steered and the cross-track error (NTUN), and the position controller (PSCN, PSCE, PIDN, PIDE) when it is active, at 10 Hz - for tuning waypoint navigation. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_128:
**IMU**: accelerometer and gyro readings (IMU) every main loop, vibration (VIBE) at 10 Hz, barometer (BARO), airspeed and the gyro FFT. Needed for vibration analysis. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_256:
**Mission commands**: each mission item as it starts in Auto mode (CMD) - shows when the vehicle reached which waypoint. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_512:
**Battery monitor**: voltage, current, consumed capacity and temperature of every battery monitor (BAT), and cell voltages where reported (BCL), plus the board's own supply (POWR) and processor temperature (MCU). Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_1024:
**Rangefinder**: rangefinder distances (RFND) and proximity sensor distances (PRX); on boats, depth readings with position (DPTH) from a downward rangefinder. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_2048:
**Compass**: the raw magnetic field of every compass (MAG) - for compass/motor interference and calibration problems. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_4096:
**Camera**: camera trigger events with position and attitude (CAM, TRIG) and the gimbal's angles (MNT). Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_8192:
**Steering**: steering input and output, desired and actual lateral acceleration and turn rate (STER) at 10 Hz - for tuning the steering controller. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_16384:
**RC input/output**: the RC receiver's channels (RCIN, RCI2), the output to motors and servos (RCOU), the received signal strength (RSSI) and the wheel encoders (WENC) at 10 Hz. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_524288:
**Raw IMU**: every single accelerometer and gyro sample at the sensor's full rate, before filtering (GYR, ACC) - for filter and vibration analysis. Makes the log very large very quickly; switch it on only for a test run, ideally on an SD card with plenty of space. Off by default. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-raw-imu-logging.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_1048576:
**Video stabilization**: gyro, acceleration and attitude every main loop (VSTB) for stabilising video afterwards with software such as Gyroflow. Off by default. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-gyroflow.html>
fields.log_settings.log_bit_2097152:
**Optical flow**: the optical flow sensor's flow rates and quality (OF). Off by default. Logged while logging runs (armed, or always with *Log while disarmed*).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-logs.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_1:
**Number of satellites**: the GPS must see at least 6 satellites. Message: *GPS numsats 4 (needs 6)*. Not scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_2:
**HDoP**: the satellite geometry (horizontal dilution of precision) must be 2.5 or better. Message: *GPS HDOP 3.1 (needs 2.5)*. Not scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_4:
**Speed error**: the speed accuracy the GPS reports must be 1.0 m/s or better. Message: *GPS speed error 1.4 (needs < 1.0)*. Scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_8:
**Position error**: the position accuracy the GPS reports must be 5 m or better horizontally and 7.5 m vertically (only checked if the GPS reports it). Messages: *GPS horiz error 6.1m (needs 5.0)*, *GPS vert error ...*. Scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_16:
**Yaw error**: the compass heading must agree with the EKF (the magnetometer innovations within their limits) - with a wrong heading GPS can't be used. Message: *Mag yaw error x=1.3 y=0.8*. Fix: calibrate the compass, check its orientation, keep it away from magnets and power wiring. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_32:
**Position drift**: standing still, the GPS position must move less than 3 m (filtered over 10 s: a 0.3 m/s average drift or a single 3 m jump). Message: *GPS drift 4.2m (needs 3.0)*. Only checked while the vehicle is on the ground and still, so on a moving boat untick it. Scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_64:
**Vertical speed**: standing still, the vertical speed the GPS reports must stay below 0.3 m/s (filtered). Message: *GPS vertical speed 0.45m/s (needs 0.30)*. Only for GPS types that report a vertical speed. Scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>
fields.gps.gps_check_128:
**Horizontal speed**: standing still, the GPS ground speed must stay below 0.3 m/s (filtered). Message: *GPS horizontal speed ...*. Untick when starting from a moving platform (e.g. a boat). Scaled by *Accepted GPS error*. All ticked checks must pass for 10 s before EKF3 uses the GPS.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-prearm-safety-checks.html>

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.barometer.baro_probe_16384:
**AUAV** (Amphenol absolute pressure sensor): looked for on the I2C bus(es) chosen below at I2C address 0x27. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-baro-external.html>
fields.distance_sensors.avoid_source_1:
**The fence**: stop before the geofence (`FENCE_*`, set up in the *Failsafes* step) instead of crossing it and triggering the fence action. Needs the fence enabled. Rover slows down and stops (or slides along / backs away, see *Avoidance behaviour*) in Acro, Steering, Loiter, Guided, Circle, Follow, Dock and Simple modes - not in Manual or Hold, and not while driving to waypoints (that is the path planner's job, `OA_TYPE`).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-object-avoidance.html>
fields.distance_sensors.avoid_source_2:
**Proximity sensors**: stop before obstacles a proximity sensor reports (`PRX*_TYPE`, e.g. a 360-degree lidar, or rangefinders fed in by the proximity type *RangeFinder*), keeping *Avoidance margin* away. Rover slows down and stops (or slides along / backs away, see *Avoidance behaviour*) in Acro, Steering, Loiter, Guided, Circle, Follow, Dock and Simple modes - not in Manual or Hold, and not while driving to waypoints (that is the path planner's job, `OA_TYPE`).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-object-avoidance.html>
fields.distance_sensors.avoid_source_4:
**The beacon fence**: with an indoor positioning system (beacons such as Marvelmind, `BCN_TYPE`), stay inside the polygon the beacons span. Rover slows down and stops (or slides along / backs away, see *Avoidance behaviour*) in Acro, Steering, Loiter, Guided, Circle, Follow, Dock and Simple modes - not in Manual or Hold, and not while driving to waypoints (that is the path planner's job, `OA_TYPE`).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-object-avoidance.html>
fields.ekf_sources.ekf_imu1:
Run an EKF3 instance (a *lane*) on **IMU 1** (the accelerometer/gyro ArduPilot numbers 1). Each ticked IMU gets its own instance; ArduPilot uses the healthiest one and switches lanes if an IMU fails - so tick every IMU the board has. Each instance costs memory and CPU: if there isn't enough, EKF3 doesn't start, then untick one. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-apm-navigation-extended-kalman-filter-overview.html>
fields.ekf_sources.ekf_imu2:
Run an EKF3 instance (a *lane*) on **IMU 2** (the accelerometer/gyro ArduPilot numbers 2). Each ticked IMU gets its own instance; ArduPilot uses the healthiest one and switches lanes if an IMU fails - so tick every IMU the board has. Each instance costs memory and CPU: if there isn't enough, EKF3 doesn't start, then untick one. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-apm-navigation-extended-kalman-filter-overview.html>
fields.ekf_sources.ekf_imu3:
Run an EKF3 instance (a *lane*) on **IMU 3** (the accelerometer/gyro ArduPilot numbers 3). Each ticked IMU gets its own instance; ArduPilot uses the healthiest one and switches lanes if an IMU fails - so tick every IMU the board has. Each instance costs memory and CPU: if there isn't enough, EKF3 doesn't start, then untick one. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-apm-navigation-extended-kalman-filter-overview.html>
fields.remote_id.did_option_1:
**Enforce Remote ID arming checks**: arming is refused until Remote ID is ready - `DID_ENABLE` set, a UA type in the Basic ID, the operator location known, and the module reporting *ready to arm* (ARM_STATUS and SYSTEM messages from the ground station / module no older than 3 s). Messages: *UA_TYPE required in BasicID*, *operator location must be set*, *ARM_STATUS not available*, or the module's own reason. Required where Remote ID is mandatory.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-remoteid.html>
fields.remote_id.did_option_2:
**No emergency status without GPS**: normally, driving armed without a GPS fix makes Remote ID broadcast an *emergency* status. Tick this when the vehicle deliberately works without GPS (indoors, beacons, visual odometry). It does *not* affect arming.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-remoteid.html>
fields.remote_id.did_option_4:
**Lock the UAS ID**: the first serial-number Basic ID received from the Remote ID module is stored permanently in the flight controller's persistent storage (with its ID and UA type); from then on that ID is used, and the module can't be swapped for one with another ID. The lock survives parameter resets and firmware updates. ArduPilot clears this option itself once the ID is locked. Only tick it if your regulator or manufacturer requires it.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-remoteid.html>
fields.generator.gen_option_1:
**Suppress maintenance-required warnings**: a RichenPower generator reports when its service interval is due; ArduPilot then repeats *Generator: requires maintenance* every 60 s while disarmed. Tick this to silence it (e.g. until the service is done). Only the RichenPower driver uses this option.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-richenpower-generator.html>
fields.scripting.scr_dir_1:
**Built-in scripts (ROMFS)**: run the scripts compiled into the firmware (only custom firmware builds have any). Unticked sets the *ROMFS* bit of `SCR_DIR_DISABLE`. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_dir_2:
**Scripts from the SD card**: run the .lua files in APM/scripts on the SD card - where your own and downloaded scripts go. Unticked sets the *APM/scripts* bit of `SCR_DIR_DISABLE`. Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_debug_1:
**Message if no scripts are running**: sends *Lua: No scripts to run* (every second) when no script is loaded, and *Scripting: stopped* when the scripting engine stops - helps to find out why a script doesn't start. Debug-level messages: the ground station may need to show those.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_debug_2:
**Runtime messages**: after every script run sends *Lua: Time: ... Mem: ... + ...* (run time in microseconds, total memory and memory used by the run) to the ground station - many messages, for debugging only.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_debug_4:
**Don't log scripts**: normally the contents of every loaded script is copied into the log, so a log shows exactly which scripts ran. Tick this to leave them out (smaller logs, or to keep scripts private).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_debug_8:
**Log runtime memory and execution time**: writes each script run's name, run time and memory use to the log (SCR) - the logged counterpart of *Runtime messages*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.scripting.scr_debug_16:
**Disable the scripting pre-arm check**: normally arming is refused when scripting failed to start, ran out of memory, a script stopped with an error, or the scripts' checksums don't match `SCR_LD_CHECKSUM` / `SCR_RUN_CHECKSUM` (messages start with *Scripting:*). Ticked, the vehicle arms anyway - a failed safety script would then go unnoticed.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-lua-scripts.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_sails:
Sets `SAIL_ENABLE` = 1 (unticked: 0) and shows the **Sails** and **Wind vane** steps. ArduPilot sails boats and land yachts alike. The other sailing settings appear after a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-home.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_motor:
Ticked when an output drives a motor (throttle, or left/right motors). With a motor, ArduPilot can motor when the wind is too light (`SAIL_WNDSPD_MIN`) and a switch can choose never / assist / always. Without one, the Motor output step and the drive tests that need throttle are skipped.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_torqeedo:
A Torqeedo electric outboard controlled over its RS485 bus: shows the **Torqeedo motor** step. Unticked sets its type to 0.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.vehicle_type.has_depth_sounder:
An echosounder (a rangefinder pointing down): shows the **Depth sounder** step. ArduPilot then logs the depth with the position and reports it to the ground station.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>
fields.vehicle_type.FRAME_CLASS:
*Rover* for vehicles on land, *Boat* for boats. A boat holds its position at the end of a mission and wherever Guided, RTL and SmartRTL arrive (it would drift otherwise), never uses its own movement to estimate the heading, and reports the water depth. The wizard's texts follow this choice. A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.steering_output.MOT_VEC_ANGLEMAX:
For a boat whose steering servo turns the motor itself (an outboard, a jet nozzle): the angle the motor turns at full steering. ArduPilot then works out the steering from the thrust direction, which steers much better at low throttle. Leave 0 for a rudder separate from the motor.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/rover-vectored-thrust.html>
fields.gps.GPS_NAVFILTER:
The motion model a u-blox receiver filters its position with. *Sea* suits boats at sea level - it assumes zero altitude, so not for lakes or rivers in the mountains (use *Automotive* there).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/boat-configuration.html>
fields.sails.sail_actuator:
Sail winch: SERVOx_FUNCTION 89 (Main Sail). Wing sail elevator: 128 - trim so the wing has zero angle of attack, MIN/MAX at maximum lift on either tack. Mast rotation: 137 - the servo turns the wing directly.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.sail_output:
The servo output the sail actuator is connected to. Apply gives it the actuator's function and takes the sail functions from every other output. *Test -* / *Test +* drive the sail output to its lowest / highest position for 3 s with ArduPilot's motor test (the vehicle is **armed** meanwhile - needs calibrated RC and passing arming checks).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.rev_mainsail:
Tick if *Test -* lets the sail out instead of pulling it in (a wing or mast: if it turns to the wrong side).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.min_mainsail:
Sail output: the pulse at the *-* end - a winch: sail pulled in to the centre line. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.max_mainsail:
Sail output: the pulse at the *+* end - a winch: sail let out to the shrouds. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.trim_mainsail:
Sail output: the centre pulse - only used by a wing sail elevator and a mast rotation (zero angle of attack). *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.rev_wingsail:
Tick if *Test -* lets the sail out instead of pulling it in (a wing or mast: if it turns to the wrong side).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.min_wingsail:
Sail output: the pulse at the *-* end - a winch: sail pulled in to the centre line. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.max_wingsail:
Sail output: the pulse at the *+* end - a winch: sail let out to the shrouds. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.trim_wingsail:
Sail output: the centre pulse - only used by a wing sail elevator and a mast rotation (zero angle of attack). *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.rev_mast:
Tick if *Test -* lets the sail out instead of pulling it in (a wing or mast: if it turns to the wrong side).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.min_mast:
Sail output: the pulse at the *-* end - a winch: sail pulled in to the centre line. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.max_mast:
Sail output: the pulse at the *+* end - a winch: sail let out to the shrouds. *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.trim_mast:
Sail output: the centre pulse - only used by a wing sail elevator and a mast rotation (zero angle of attack). *+* / *-* change it by 10 us and move the sail there with the motor test.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.sail_reboot:
ArduPilot shows its sailing settings only after `SAIL_ENABLE` is set and the flight controller has rebooted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_ANGLE_MIN:
Sheet pulled in completely: the angle between the centre line and the boom.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_ANGLE_MAX:
Sheet let out completely: the angle between the centre line and the boom (at the shrouds, about 90 deg).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_ANGLE_IDEAL:
The angle the sail keeps to the apparent wind the wind vane reports, until it reaches either end. 0 keeps the boom parallel to the vane. Raise it if the sail flaps. Test it in Acro.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-hardware.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_HEEL_MAX:
Above this heel the heel controller lets the sail out (it never pulls it in). Either a low limit with a small I gain - the sail eases out gradually - or the real maximum heel with higher gains.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.ATC_SAIL_P:
Most of the heel control comes from P and I. Watch the effect in Acro by heeling the vehicle.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.ATC_SAIL_I:
A low I with a low maximum heel eases the sail out gradually. Watch the effect in Acro by heeling the vehicle.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.ATC_SAIL_IMAX:
How much of the sail output the I term may use (0..1). Watch the effect in Acro by heeling the vehicle.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_NO_GO_ANGLE:
The vehicle can't sail closer to the wind than this; heading upwind it sails at this angle and tacks. Used in every wind - set it with that in mind.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_XTRACK_MAX:
Sailing upwind in Auto, the vehicle tacks when it is this far off the line between waypoints - a corridor twice as wide. 0: it only tacks once it can reach the waypoint.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_LOIT_RADIUS:
In Loiter a sailing vehicle can't stand still: it keeps moving within this radius and tacks back to the loiter point. (Motoring, it uses LOIT_RADIUS.)

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.SAIL_WNDSPD_MIN:
Below this wind speed the motor takes over (when the motor switch is on *assist*, the setting at boot). 0: never. Needs a wind speed sensor.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.tack_switch:
An RC switch that makes the vehicle tack (`RCx_OPTION` = 63) in Acro and Auto, when heading upwind.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.mainsail_channel:
In Manual the throttle stick drives the motor and - without a channel of its own - the sail as well. Give the sail its own RC channel (`RCx_OPTION` = 207) to control the two separately.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.sails.motor_switch:
A three-position switch (`RCx_OPTION` = 74): low = never use the motor, middle = assist (in light wind and to help a slow tack), high = always motor (no tacking).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/sailboat-configure.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_TYPE:
*Heading when armed*: no sensor - the wind is assumed to come from straight ahead of the vehicle at arming; *... offset by an RC knob*: the same, turned up to ±45 deg by an RC channel. *Analog*: a potentiometer vane. *NMEA 0183*: a serial wind sensor (MWV sentence). A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.wind_reboot:
ArduPilot shows the wind vane settings only after the type is set and the flight controller has rebooted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.wind_offset_channel:
The RC channel (`RCx_OPTION` = 97) whose knob turns the assumed wind direction by up to ±45 deg.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-home-heading.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_PIN:
The analog input the vane's wiper is connected to (e.g. 15 = Pixhawk ADC 6.6 V, 103 = Pixhawk SBUS). Pull it down with about 100 kOhm: the wiper floats between the potentiometer's ends.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-analogue.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_V_MIN:
Set by *Calibrate direction* (recommended) - or enter the vane's voltage range yourself.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-analogue.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_V_MAX:
Set by *Calibrate direction* (recommended) - or enter the vane's voltage range yourself.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-analogue.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_DZ:
The angle where the potentiometer jumps from its highest to its lowest voltage (from its data sheet).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-analogue.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_OFS:
Corrects how the sensor is turned on the vehicle: with the vane pointing at the bow, the wind direction must read 0. *Set headwind offset* works it out.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-analogue.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_DIR_FILT:
Smooths the direction. Lower it if the vehicle reacts to every gust when sailing upwind - the sail then reacts more slowly too.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_SPEED_TYPE:
*Airspeed sensor*: a pitot tube (on the vane, pointing into the wind; keep ARSPD_USE and ARSPD_AUTOCAL at 0). *Modern Devices rev. P*: a hot-wire sensor on two analog pins. *Cup anemometer*: on RPM sensor 1, RPM1_SCALING set to give m/s. *NMEA 0183*: the wind sensor's MWV sentence. A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_SPEED_PIN:
Analog input of the sensor's OUT pin (3.3 V input; power the sensor with 10-12 V).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-MD-rev-p.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_TEMP_PIN:
Analog input of the sensor's TMP pin; -1 without it (room temperature is assumed, slightly less accurate).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-MD-rev-p.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_SPEED_OFS:
The sensor's voltage in still air - set by *Calibrate zero wind speed*.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-MD-rev-p.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_SPEED_MIN:
Below this apparent wind speed the vane's direction is ignored (a vane may stick in light air). If the wind is always below it, the vehicle never learns the direction.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_SPEED_FILT:
Smooths the apparent wind speed.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.WNDVN_TRUE_FILT:
Smooths the true wind speed and direction.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane.html>
fields.wind_vane.wind_port:
The serial port of the NMEA wind sensor: Apply sets its protocol to WindVane (21) and the baud rate below. NMEA 0183 uses RS-422 - connect it through a converter.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-NMEA.html>
fields.wind_vane.wind_baud:
The sensor's baud rate - NMEA 0183 normally 4800 (see the sensor's manual).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/wind-vane-NMEA.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_type:
*Tiller connector*: the autopilot replaces the tiller at the Torqeedo battery. *Motor connector*: it talks to the motor directly. A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_reboot:
ArduPilot shows the Torqeedo settings only after the type is set and the flight controller has rebooted.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_port:
The serial port of the RS485 converter: Apply sets its protocol to Torqeedo (39) and 19200 baud - the only rate the motor speaks.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_onoff_pin:
Switches the motor on (tiller connection, through a MOSFET). *The serial port's flow-control pin* uses its RTS pin. A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_de_pin:
Drives the converter's DE/RE pins (send/receive). *The serial port's flow-control pin* uses its CTS pin. A change needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_servo_fn:
The output function the motor follows: *Throttle*, or the left/right motor of a twin-motor boat.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_power:
Limits the motor's power (motor connection only).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_slew:
The throttle may rise from 0 to 100 % no faster than this - gentler on the drive train; 0 = no limit.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_dir_delay:
Output stays at zero this long when changing between forward and reverse.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_option_1:
Writes the motor's reports to the log (TRQD, and TRST/TRSE or TRMP).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_option_2:
Also sends the motor's reports to the ground station as text messages.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_battery:
Sets `BATT_MONITOR` = 23: voltage and current come from the Torqeedo battery or motor (then skip the analog battery monitor setup). Needs a **reboot**.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.torqeedo.trq_clear_switch:
An RC switch (`RCx_OPTION` = 156) that clears the motor's error codes.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-torqeedo.html>
fields.depth_sounder.depth_rangefinder:
Which of ArduPilot's ten rangefinders is the depth sounder: the one already pointing down, else the first one not in use.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>
fields.depth_sounder.depth_model:
The echosounders ArduPilot documents. *Fill in* fills in type, baud rate and range from the documentation; nothing is written before Apply.

fields.depth_sounder.depth_type:
The rangefinder driver: *NMEA* for most echosounders, *BlueRoboticsPing* for the Ping sonar. A change needs a **reboot**.

fields.depth_sounder.depth_port:
The serial port of the echosounder: Apply sets its protocol to Rangefinder (9) and the baud rate below.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>
fields.depth_sounder.depth_baud:
Must match the echosounder's own setting (see its manual).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>

Readings below this depth are ignored.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>
fields.depth_sounder.depth_max:
Readings beyond this depth are ignored - the sounder's own range.

Readings beyond this depth are ignored (older firmware: in cm).

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/common-underwater-sonars-landingpage.html>
fields.boat_loiter.LOIT_RADIUS:
Within this distance of its target the boat simply drifts. Small = holds tighter, but uses the motor more often.

ArduPilot documentation: <https://ardupilot.org/rover/docs/loiter-mode.html>
fields.boat_loiter.LOIT_TYPE:
Only matters once the boat has drifted outside the radius: *forward or backward* turns least, *bow first* suits boats that handle badly in reverse or a forward-facing sensor, *stern first* keeps the bow away from the target.
